entities.summary:
Theon of Smyrna was a Greek philosopher and mathematician who lived in the 2nd century CE. Born in the city of Smyrna, he was a prominent figure in the Pythagorean school of thought. His surviving works, such as his treatise on mathematics, had a significant impact on the development of Greek mathematics and philosophy.

Theon's mathematical treatises were influential in shaping the understanding of Plato's works, making him a key figure in the transmission of ancient Greek knowledge. His works were also studied by later scholars, including the Byzantine mathematician John Philoponus. 

Theon's legacy extends beyond his own works, as his contributions to Greek mathematics and philosophy laid the groundwork for later scientific developments. Theon's emphasis on the importance of mathematics in understanding the natural world influenced the work of later scholars, including the ancient Greek physician Galen. 

Theon of Smyrna's life and work are a testament to the enduring power of ancient Greek knowledge and the importance of preserving and studying the works of ancient scholars.
